name: awk
summary: Processes text column by column with a small language.
description: awk reads text line by line and splits each line into fields: $1 is the first column, $2 the second, $0 the whole line, NF the number of fields and NR the line number. An awk program is a series of “pattern { action }” blocks: the action runs on the lines that match the pattern. BEGIN and END blocks run before and after reading.

options.description: Field separator (default: spaces and tabs). -F: for /etc/passwd, -F, for a simple CSV.
Sets a variable before running: -v limit=100.
Reads the awk program from a file instead of the command line.

arguments.name: PROGRAM
arguments.description: awk program, in single quotes so the shell leaves $1, $2… alone. Example: '{print $1}'.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: File(s) to process. Without a file: standard input.

examples.explanation: Prints the first column of each line (here the client’s IP address).
With “:” as the separator, prints each user’s name and shell.
With no action, awk prints the lines whose 3rd column is over 100.

examples.command: awk '{ total += $2 } END { print total }' sales.txt
examples.explanation: Adds up the 2nd column and prints the total at the end.
Skips the header line (NR > 1) and prints each process’s PID and command.
